course_description:
Second supervised practice experience in a social welfare agency. The course focuses on integration of practice experience with course material and companion courses.

Ensure you carefully read the 2026 Social Work Practice Education Guide . This contains all essential information regarding your placement and UQ requirements.

You can access the Guide HERE.

You have reached the final stage of your program and stand at the threshold of professional practice. The skills and interests you have been developing, the work you have done, and the sacrifices you have made to get this far will come into their own over the next few months.

Make the most of this final placement!

The clearer you are about your own goals for the placement, and how they link with the Learning Objectives of the course overall, the more likely it is that you will have a positive and constructive experience.

The School and the Practice Education Team are committed to supporting you through this challenging, exciting time.

Additional timetable information
This course has a calendar variation because the placement starts before the beginning of semester. For this reason the weeks in this profile use different weeks, where Week 1 is the first week of placement. That is, the weeks in this profile are not UQ semester standard weeks
.
In order to successfully complete this placement you must do at least 500 hours. No credit is available for travel time to and from placement, sick-days or public holidays.
The placement includes
four
integration workshops on Fridays (14 August - 11 September - 9 October and 30 October), 12:00-2:00.
The workshops are held over Zoom. The link to the sessions is
HERE.
T
he Integration Workshops are mandated by the AASW as an essential part of your professional training
. As such we consider participation to be a fundamental aspect of all social work programs. They offer you an opportunity to reflect on your field experiences and to interact with highly skilled social workers (as well as your student colleagues) in a supportive environment. The Integration Workshops are where you consolidate your learning.
Your attendance is strongly encouraged.
Students who attend each session
with their camera on
may count the two hours of the session towards placement.
For all information regarding placement attendance, see the
Social Work Practice Education Guide 2026
course_aims:
SWSP7266 aims to afford students ﾠthe opportunity to develop and demonstrate the skills and knowledge appropriate to Australian social work practice at a new-graduate level within the context of an existing social work service.

Upon successfully completing SWSP7266, students will be able to demonstrate they are 'competent, effective, skilled, knowledge-based, ethically aware and confident practitioners'.ﾠ

As per the AASW accreditation guidelines, students will 'have a commitment to social justice and social change in the interests of the citizens of their society, recognising that there are competing views of desirable approaches to the organisation of society and the provision of social services. They will have the ability to think critically and reflectively about their practice, and a commitment to intervene in the interests of the client groups they serve.'

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate the consistent application of the AASW Code of Ethics (2020) to all aspects of practice in the placement agency, identifying and responding to ethical dilemmas as they arise.
Contribute to the placement organisation’s respectful incorporation of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultural and experiential knowledge in both practice and service design.
Demonstrate the ability to develop in collaboration with clients, and undertake, interventions informed by anti-oppressive principles addressing both individual and structural concerns.
Articulate critical reflections on the impact of personal perspectives and organisational policies into the needs of clients with diverse cultural and personal identities.
Articulate a developed, reflective practice framework incorporating an evidence-informed, client focused and critical perspective applicable across multiple practice fields.
Critically review professional decisions to identify challenges between client-led outcomes and professional, holistic assessments.
Maintain professionalism, demonstrating evidence-informed knowledge of the field while actively engaging with and seeking out learning and development opportunities.

Proactively arrange, prepare for and prioritise regular professional supervision in which themes of critical reflection on practice, the use of self and positional power are topics of discussion in the context of a balanced agenda of education, support and accountability.

assessment_details.title: Mid-point Evaluation
assessment_details.task_description: At the approximate mid-point of the placement, the supervisor is asked to complete, and submit to the University, a mid-placement review. This will fall around week 8 of your placement. Note that this is an approximate date only: individual placement circumstances will vary. Dates and times should be negotiated with your Supervisor. This is the student's responsibility. This provides a basis for identifying the extent of your progress and any specific learning tasks that need to be completed in the remaining portion of the placement to assist you to pass the placement. The review evaluates your performance against the Learning Curriculum and the course Learning Objectives. A template to be used in the review is available in Learning Resources on the course Blackboard site. A PDF of the evaluation report, signed and dated by the Supervisor and co-signed/dated by the Student, must be uploaded to Turnitin by the student. See the Social Work Practice Education Guide 2026 (sec. 4.5.1) for detailed information regarding placement evaluations. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Final Placement Evaluation
assessment_details.due_date: Must be completed prior to end of Placement.
assessment_details.task_description: At a point no later than the final week of the placement, the Supervisor is asked to complete a Final Placement Evaluation, using the template available in Learning Resources on the course Blackboard site. This will fall around week 18 of your placement. Note that this is an approximate date only: individual placement circumstances will vary. Dates and times should be negotiated with your Supervisor. This is your responsibility. The review evaluates your performance against the Learning Curriculum and the course Learning Objectives. The review should be a discussion between Student and Supervisor, in which the student's performance and development across the entirety of the placement are reflected upon and evaluated as either Pass or Fail. A PDF of the evaluation report, signed and dated by the Supervisor and the Student, will be uploaded to Turnitin by the student.
